source_review.notes: Reviewed PostgreSQL 18 system-catalog, information-schema, pg_depend, dependency-tracking, and pg_description documentation; SQLite schema-table documentation; and MySQL 8.4 information-schema documentation. All seven final destinations returned HTTP 200. Product-specific layout, visibility, dependency, and mutation statements are explicitly scoped.

evidence: Checked directed graph G=(V,E), object identity/name/namespace/kind, dependent/referenced edge direction, reverse reachability, and topological drop-order terminology.
Checked metadata observation and fingerprint notation always includes engine, database, role, snapshot, search path, and canonicalization context.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Qualified names are consistently treated as resolution/presentation values rather than universal stable identity.

evidence: Recomputed six unique object identifiers and six unique namespace/name/kind triples.
Recomputed contiguous two-column ordinals for customer, customer_read, and orders.
Recomputed customer reverse closure as customer_pk, customer_read, order_customer_fk, and customer while retaining orders.
Recomputed analyst visibility as exactly app, customer, and customer_read.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The fixture counts are finite model evidence only, not a production catalog inventory.

evidence: Re-derived restrict behavior from nonempty reverse dependency edges.
Re-derived cascade closure by transitive reverse reachability and dependents-before-referenced ordering.
Re-derived why a canonical digest detects representation change but neither identifies the correct side nor proves semantic equivalence.
Re-derived privilege-filtered absence as an observation-context result rather than universal nonexistence.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Real dependency flavors and namespace collision rules remain engine-defined.

evidence: Reviewed empty catalogs, duplicate/reused identities, duplicate qualified keys, missing dependency targets, noncontiguous ordinals, and dependency cycles.
Reviewed quoted names, schemas/search paths, rename versus drop/recreate, hidden/dropped/system columns, and composite-column order.
Reviewed dynamic SQL, external consumers, privilege filtering, mixed snapshots, major-version changes, unknown object kinds, direct catalog writes, and malicious stored DDL text.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The model deliberately does not simulate engine dependency flavors, DDL concurrency, grant closure, or dynamic references.

evidence: Validated unique identities, unique namespace/name/kind keys, and existing dependency targets.
Validated ordinal sequences equal 1 through column count in declared order.
Validated acyclicity with visiting/visited sets and detected the injected 10-to-20-to-10 cycle.
Validated deterministic recursive drop planning and deterministic canonical digest construction.
The verifier matched exact eight-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status.
invariant_checking.notes: The uniform-edge planner is not generalized to normal, automatic, internal, extension, partition, shared, or pinned engine dependencies.

evidence: Reviewed dependency direction and reverse-closure derivation against restrict/cascade semantics.
Reviewed dependents-before-referenced order against every induced fixture edge.
Reviewed cycle detection termination and the need for grouped/rejected handling outside a DAG.
Reviewed fingerprint stability/change arguments against deterministic ordering and included fields.
proof_review.notes: No proof is claimed for a specific engine's complete catalog or destructive DDL implementation.

evidence: Separated portable information-schema concepts from native catalog implementation details.
Separated durable schema metadata, approximate planner statistics, runtime telemetry, and external replicated catalogs.
Separated database-recorded dependencies from dynamic SQL and external application dependencies.
Separated hash equality/difference evidence from semantic correctness and authorization claims.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No absence, drift, or safe-cascade claim is generalized beyond its observation and dependency scope.

evidence: The standard-library catalog-graph model executed successfully through the repository verifier.
All seven final official reference destinations returned HTTP 200 on 2026-08-30.
Structure, front matter, local links, ten examples, five exercises, five answers, and exact snippet expectations passed draft validation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, DDL transaction, catalog migration, privilege audit, external catalog, or production cascade was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter consistently treats catalogs as typed relational control-plane state and connects identity, namespace, structure, dependencies, visibility, versions, fingerprints, and supported DDL.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed portable/native adapter boundaries, safe joins, ordinal reconstruction, impact plans, dynamic dependency gaps, least-privilege inventory, snapshot/version recording, drift evidence, upgrade handling, and direct-mutation prohibition.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet, graph model, ten distinct examples, and five retrieval-to-transfer exercises progress from catalog vocabulary through destructive planning and production drift auditing.

limitations: Internal authoring, official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model do not certify any live engine catalog, information-schema completeness, role visibility, DDL transaction, dependency closure, cascade safety, schema fingerprint, migration, major-version adapter, external lineage catalog, or production fitness.
